candidates.name: staphyloxanthin biosynthesis
candidates.scope: Nine native reaction nodes, six proteins; farnesyl diphosphate through final glycosylated branched-C15 acylated pigment, including AldH.
candidates.limitations: Native activated sugar/acyl donor identities are inferred; primary KCTC1928 cloning/RN4220 deletion versus strain-specific protein annotation requires care. Engineered E. coli produces fatty-acyl analogs, not exact native pigment.

candidates.name: aerobactin biosynthetic process
candidates.scope: IucD lysine N6-hydroxylation, IucB acetylation, IucA first and IucC second citrate ligations; transport separate.
candidates.limitations: Retrieve exact native pathway body and full primary methods; ATP product convention must follow current mechanistic evidence. MIBiG Grimontia/Vibrio clusters do not establish E. coli/Klebsiella strain claims.

candidates.name: bacillibactin biosynthesis
candidates.scope: Full chorismate-to-DHB and holo-carrier/NRPS condensation with glycine and threonine, trimeric ester release; not merely existing E. coli DHB record.
candidates.limitations: Exact covalent carrier identifiers, complete native boundary and Sfp activation/strain scope need verification. 2025 reconstitution is Parageobacillus, not evidence transferable to Bacillus subtilis168.

deferred.name: bacillithiol biosynthetic process
deferred.reason: BshC cysteine ligation/activated donor chemistry remains unresolved in inspected primary leads; genetic requirement not balanced catalyst equation.

deferred.name: bacilysin biosynthesis
deferred.reason: Inspected 2013 primary distinguishes shunt tetrahydrotyrosines and unknown epoxidation step; MIBiG complete cluster flag is not complete chemical mechanism.

coverage_gaps: Prior GO-CAM/WikiPathways no-more-ready conclusion is bounded to dated yeast/model and eight-taxon caches, not all current models/releases.
MIBiG4.0 archive has only bounded canary/product-name screening; questionable quality/completeness and cluster membership cannot be treated as complete mechanisms.
DRAM1 399 module support rows have not all been semantically screened against current201 records; DRAM2 remains a separately uninspected source.
SEED selector provides additional lead labels but only narrow native canaries were assessed.
BRENDA, HADEG and dbCAN retained support tables do not themselves establish reaction order, taxa and catalyst completeness.
Previously blocked generic carrier/chemical classes may merit evidence-driven reassessment after schema changes; no blanket upgrade.
